subject: Cascade Health - request for temporary latency SLO carveout and pricing exception
messages:
From: Brynn Cole <brynn@cascadehealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cascadehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 14:12:00 -0000
Subject: Pilot needs — ask for temporary SLO relaxation + pricing for multi-region test

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to run a multi-region pilot (US + EU) for our patient-facing summarization feature. We have two asks from procurement and engineering before we can start the pilot:

1) A temporary latency/availability tolerance during the pilot period (6 weeks). Our infra team expects bursty traffic that can increase tail latency; we'd need a short-term SLO change from 99.95% to 99.90% for the pilot window.
2) A promotional price for the pilot terms — we were hoping for a 25% concession for the first three months while we validate the integration.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate both items? Procurement wants to capture this in the SOW if we get affirmative.

Attaching a small sample of the request traffic patterns we expect (cascade_latency_sample.csv).

Best,
Brynn
Brynn Cole
Director, Product Integrations
Cascade Health

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Brynn Cole <brynn@cascadehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pilot needs — ask for temporary SLO relaxation + pricing for multi-region test

Hi Brynn — great to see momentum here.

Quick notes:
- We can support the pilot but need deal-desk approval for the commercial concession and a limited SLO variance signed off by leadership.
- To move quickly, please confirm the pilot start date and expected daily token/embedding volume so Ben can model the cost impact.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- Week 0: finalize SOW with temporary SLO clause (pilot-only, 6 weeks).
- Week 1–6: pilot live. Redwood provides a temporary availability tolerance (99.90%) with clearly defined rollback to standard SLO.
- Post-pilot: review telemetry & decide on production SLO and pricing.

I have copied Marissa and Ben to get an expedited approval for the price concession. If you can share the procurement contact, I’ll route the SOW draft for countersignature.

Thanks,
Mateo
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 16:22:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Pilot needs — ask for temporary SLO relaxation + pricing for multi-region test

Team — reviewed the numbers attached by Cascade and ran a quick impact model. Key points and recommended guardrails before we grant any concession: 

- Pricing: a 25% discount across the board for three months is heavier than our standard pilot concessions. I can approve a 20% pilot discount as a deal-desk-level concession, but anything at 25% requires exec signoff.
- SLO carveout: we can agree to a limited SLO relaxation (99.90%) for the stated 6-week pilot, but must bind the concession to:
  * a clear rollback clause after the pilot (automatic revert to 99.95%),
  * a cap on cumulative service credits during the pilot (max of 5% of quarterly spend), and
  * telemetry handoff and a short post-mortem within 10 business days after pilot end.

Attachments: pricing-model_proposal.xlsx (projected revenue impact), Cascade_SOW_v2.pdf (draft SOW with proposed clause).

Asking Jonas for exec approval on the 25% requested discount and to clear the limited SLO carveout as written.

Ben Carter
Manager, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:58:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pilot needs — ask for temporary SLO relaxation + pricing for multi-region test

On Tue, 04 May 2027 16:22:00 +0000, ben_carter wrote:
> Team — reviewed the numbers attached by Cascade and ran a quick impact model. Key points and recommended guardrails before we grant any concession:
> 
> - Pricing: a 25% discount across the board for three months is heavier than our standard pilot concessions. I can approve a 20% pilot discount as a deal-desk-level concession, but anything at 25% requires exec signoff.
> - SLO carveout: we can agree to a limited SLO relaxation (99.90%) for the stated 6-week pilot, but must bind the concession to: ...

I reviewed the context and am comfortable providing the exec approval with conditions. Formal approval:

- Approve a one-time 25% promotional discount limited to the first six months of the contract (not three) for the Cascade Health pilot, contingent on a signed SOW and the rollback clause.
- Approve a temporary availability tolerance changing the operational SLO from 99.95% to 99.90% for the specified 6-week pilot window only.
- Require that the service-credit exposure during the pilot be capped at 5% of projected quarterly spend and that the CS/engineering handoff and a post-pilot telemetry review be completed within 10 business days.

This signoff is conditioned on: the SOW reflecting the exact pilot window and rollback, legal acceptance of the language in section 4.2 (remedies), and a final procurement countersignature. Once legal confirms redlines in the SOW, finance will issue the final concession paperwork.

Jonas Weber
Senior Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Brynn Cole <brynn@cascadehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@cascadehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: Final — pilot terms and next steps (SOW + DocuSign)

Hi Brynn and procurement team —

Thanks — we have executive approval on the two items you requested, with the guardrails Jonas outlined below. Summary of agreed items: 

- Pricing concession: 25% promotional discount applied to Redwood fees for the first six months of the contract (pilot is counted as month 0 but discount applies once contracted).
- Temporary SLO change: operational availability tolerance relaxed from 99.95% to 99.90% for the 6-week pilot window only. Automatic rollback after pilot; rollback triggers specified in SOW.
- Service-credit exposure: capped at 5% of projected quarterly spend for the duration of the pilot.
- Post-pilot telemetry review: Redwood and Cascade will complete a joint review within 10 business days of pilot completion and decide on production SLO.

Next steps:
1) I am attaching the current SOW (Cascade_SOW_v2.pdf) — please review section 4.2 (remedies) and provide any legal redlines.
2) Once procurement confirms, I will send a DocuSign for countersignature: https://www.docusign.net/transaction/abcdef123456
3) Finance will finalize the concession paperwork after legal signs off.

Attachments: Cascade_SOW_v2.pdf, pricing-model_proposal.xlsx.

Looking forward to getting the pilot started — please ping me if we need to expedite the countersignature.

Best regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
